synopsis: The Centre, days twenty-one to twenty-three. Iseul Fane stands at the rim of a hole eleven people dug in one night and takes the record in order -- who ordered it, who dug it, with what, to what depth -- and then recites the Third Article at them: every well within the bounds is the Wardenry's to open. A hole is not a well; a hole nine feet deep with water standing in it and a woman drinking out of it at dawn is something nobody has ever had to name. She tells them she has cause to break the tile, tells them so out loud in front of the hands, and gives them the second proviso for nothing: ground, not paper -- the packet goes off the ground in the hand that holds it. That night at the cairn she opens the waxed sleeve a third time in three days and reads both Articles against each other for the first time in a hundred and sixty-six years: the Second lets her break the tile on a spoken cause, the Fourth lets a master with a whole tile require the survey be begun within a season, and whichever sentence is spoken first governs. She is the only mouth between the rims that can speak either, and she tells Ysoly so rather than spring it. On the twenty-second the near-side leader on four goes down in the traces with the staggers and is cut out where she lies, and eleven people find they can bury a hask for the first time in the history of the Road, because the ground at the Centre takes a spade -- and the argument runs across the grave, and it runs by age. On the twenty-third Sabra Onn draws the hole to the clay four times and fills every butt on nine wagons, one thousand and eighty gallons out of a four-foot square, which is the volume the packet could never give; Ysoly cuts it on the water face in front of her own hands, where under the fifth head of the Compact it becomes a book of account admissible at either rim and beyond the reach of any seal. Oreth Vask rides in at dusk on four hask with the dust of thirty-six wagons standing on the north beacons behind him, prices everything, reads the word 'begun' back at them, and does not finish the last sentence. Then Iseul unwraps a lead disc that has been in cloth since RR 191, names Oreth Vask and Sabra Onn as her two witnesses, drives the pin, speaks the Fourth Article onto the ground, and names Denet Rasca the finder -- so that the Wardenry owes itself. Then she speaks the cause under the Second Article and puts her hand out for the tile.
title: Salt Law
